page.title: Day 8 against Neave's manual
page.standfirst_html: Every flag the comparator raised for Day 8, adjudicated against K.Day.8.11Jan20.pdf — the extracted text for wording, sixteen page images for numbers, structure, and the two things pdftotext cannot read reliably here: a systematic rendering of the minus sign as “!” throughout the Major Activity's tables, and a 0–5 rating-scale graphic that scrambles reading order on the three Activity pages. The headline is printed page 12: three whole source paragraphs are missing from the site (the “basic version” caveat and the “darkness phase” description), and the paragraph that survives has a wrong cross-reference (Day 1 page 27 read as page 37), a Deming quote replaced with nonsense (“transformation of Western style of management” became “This formation of a System was of management”), a fabricated sentence with no source at all, two word substitutions, and a dropped numbered list item — all in one paragraph. Decide each one; export the file; I make the edits and open the PR.

items.proposal:
[]{#sec-page12}
Now, the version of the exercise as laid out in both *DemDim* and *The New Economics* is admittedly rather basic, not to say crude! But it serves its purpose in demonstrating the main kinds of differences that result from the three phases and their consequences. So I shall stick to this basic version for the time being in order for you to see how the same results as those in either book are obtained when using the tables provided in this Activity. Then, when moving on to your own use of the exercise, I'll suggest some amendments that you might like to adopt in order to make the exercise less basic and more flexible and realistic.

The first of the three phases is the "darkness" phase; this reflects the description in Deming's paragraph reproduced on the previous page. In its decision-making and its choice of strategies, procedures and operations (for which I'll generally use the word "options"), each area is simply focused on what will be best for itself, irrespective of harm which might be caused elsewhere. It's as far away as can be imagined from the Joiner Triangle's "All One Team" and from "Cooperation: Win-Win". You might like to look back to Deming's paragraph to confirm that this is indeed the case. Such an approach is often not the "fault" of those involved in the decision-making: it is simply a consequence of the organisation's management style, culture, methods, and attitude to appraisal and to reward (or the opposite), etc.

In the second phase, there is now *some* understanding of Deming's fundamental concept of viewing the organisation as a *system*. Recall the hugely important flow diagram on [Day 1 page 35](../day-01/11-deming-story.qmd#sec-page35) which appeared on that page as the very first item in his list of "A Summary of Teachings to Top Management and to Engineers in Japan". For those in the area considering adopting a certain option, this change immediately refocuses their attention from being wholly concerned with the effect of that option *within* their own area to also appreciating its likely effects *elsewhere* in the organisation. Even though the option appears likely to be beneficial *within*, should it unfortunately appear likely to be too detrimental *elsewhere* then that option will now be rejected (whereas it would have been happily accepted during the first phase). The consequence of this change of attitude is twofold: (a) less options are now adopted than would have been the case in the first phase, thus involving less work, disruption and change, and yet (b) the organisation as a whole is better off than it would have been if the options initially being considered had all been adopted. Sounds like win-win to me!

So what's the third phase? This is the one that really reflects Deming's phrase (see [Day 1 page 27](../day-01/09-different.qmd#sec-page27)): "transformation of Western style of management" (although the style of management that could do with transformation is hardly unique to the West!). In the second phase, although the various areas now also consider the likely effects of their proposals elsewhere in the organisation, they are still *only* considering possibilities that appear directly *advantageous to their own area*. What's new in the third phase is that they also start to consider options which, on the face of it, are *disadvantageous* to their own area but will still be adopted if the gains elsewhere warrant it. The exercise demonstrates that this produces yet further gains for the organisation as a whole. An obvious example is where Purchasing now decides to buy something more expensive than before if its superior quality and reliability etc are worth it.

So let's now take a look at the tables provided in this Major Activity. As I mentioned on [page 10, above](05-introduction-to-the-major-activity.qmd#sec-page10), there are similarities with, but also differences from, the tables in *DemDim*. To avoid confusion you may therefore now largely prefer to ignore the book version: to help you do that, where there are such differences I'll now mostly place references to them in brackets. Also to help reduce any confusion, in future I shall:

(i) refer to the *DemDim* tables by their Figure numbers 43–48, not their Table numbers 1–6; and

(ii) refer to the table numbers here in words, i.e. Table One, Table Two, …, up to Table Five.

*DemDim* Figure 43 is simply a blank sheet, merely showing that this particular use of the exercise involves just three areas. So I haven't wasted space here by including a version of that blank sheet. The first table to be provided here, Table One (see the next page), is essentially the same as *DemDim* Figure 44. In the Major Activity you will be using full-page versions of these tables. During this introduction I shall use small
items.evidence_html:
Confirmed on the page image, printed p12 (and p11 for the paragraph immediately before it) — this is one continuous run of corruption across the whole page:
  1. Three whole source paragraphs are missing, not paraphrased: the “this basic version, admittedly crude” caveat, the “darkness” phase description, and the second-phase paragraph about the Day 1 page 35 flow diagram (Missing Gap 3, 4; the second-phase paragraph scores as Altered 24 rather than Missing only because one clause within it happened to clear the 40% floor against an unrelated sentence).
  2. The one paragraph that does survive is itself corrupted: the cross-reference reads “Day 1 page 37” where Neave's own text says “page 27” (linking to the wrong file and the wrong section entirely — 11-deming-story.qmd#sec-page37 instead of 09-different.qmd#sec-page27, confirmed by locating the actual quote there); the quoted phrase “transformation of Western style of management” became the nonsensical “This formation of a System was of management”; and the parenthetical aside was rewritten into something that doesn't parse (“oh-so familiar makes it so barely a case for the Word” for “hardly unique to the West!”).
  3. Two plain word substitutions: “warrant”→“exceed” and “the exercise”→“the process”, both changing the meaning of otherwise-intact sentences.
  4. The paragraph's last sentence is fabricated — “No ulterior motive or secret!” has no counterpart anywhere in the PDF (scores 15% corpus-wide, Unsourced 4) — and replaces the source's actual closing example ("An obvious example is where Purchasing now decides to buy something more expensive..."), itself garbled beyond recovery in the current site text ("Purchasing now decides to try something more expensive that betters it the superior quality and reliability are worth it.").
  5. List item (ii) is missing entirely — the site has “(i) ... Table numbers 1–6; and” with nothing following, though the sentence explicitly promises a numbered list of two.
  6. The sentence introducing that list is itself garbled (“To perhaps aid your first steps, may I now briefly signify to ignore the book version” for “To avoid confusion you may therefore now largely prefer to ignore the book version”).
  7. Two final word swaps: “mainly”→“merely” and “the particular”→“this particular”.
The proposal restores the source in full, preserving the site's existing working links (page 10 above, and the Day 1 links moved to their correct anchors) and the italics visible on the page image (some, system, within ×2, elsewhere ×2, only, advantageous to their own area, disadvantageous) that the current corrupted text had already partly lost. This is the pass's one big finding — please read it in full before deciding.
